item.title: Iran's nuclear chief rejects enrichment curbs ahead of Islamabad talks
item.description:
Iran's nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami on Thursday dismissed demands to curtail the country's uranium enrichment program, calling such efforts futile just days before high-stakes negotiations with the United States are set to begin in Pakistan's capital.

Speaking on the sidelines of a memorial service marking 40 days since the death of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Eslami said that "the claims and demands of our enemies to restrict Iran's enrichment programme are merely wishes that will be buried," according to Iran's ISNA news agency. He added that no law or external pressure could halt Iran's nuclear progress and that demands to abandon enrichment were "nonsensical".

item.title: UK forces Russian submarines to retreat from undersea cables
item.description:
Britain on Thursday revealed it had tracked three Russian submarines conducting covert operations near undersea cables and pipelines in waters north of the UK, in a month-long surveillance campaign that ended with all three vessels retreating toward Russia.

Defence Secretary John Healey said British forces identified an Akula-class nuclear attack submarine entering international waters in the High North several weeks ago and quickly determined it was deployed as a distraction while two submarines from Russia's Main Directorate of Deep Sea Research, known as GUGI, carried out what the Ministry of Defence described as "nefarious activity" near critical underwater infrastructure.

item.title: Iran demands Bitcoin tolls for Hormuz tanker passage
item.description: Despite a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran announced Tuesday evening, Tehran is pressing ahead with demands that oil tankers pay tolls in Bitcoin and other digital currencies to transit the Strait of Hormuz, raising doubts about whether the critical waterway will see a meaningful return of commercial shipping anytime soon.

item.title: Iran envoy deletes post on Islamabad delegation amid ceasefire rift
item.description:
Iran's Ambassador to Pakistan, Reza Amiri Moghadam, deleted a post on X late Thursday announcing that an Iranian delegation would arrive in Islamabad that evening for talks with the United States, raising fresh uncertainty about whether high-stakes negotiations set for Friday will go ahead as planned.

Moghadam had written that "despite skepticism of Iranian public opinion due to repeated ceasefire violations by Israeli regime to sabotage the diplomatic initiative," the delegation would arrive Thursday night at the invitation of Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for "serious talks based on 10 points proposed by Iran," according to Moneycontrol, which published the text of the post before it was removed. The post was subsequently deleted, Xinhua International reported, though no official explanation was given.

item.title: Netanyahu rejects cease-fire calls, vows strikes on Hezbollah
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated on Thursday that there is no ceasefire in Lebanon, defying international calls to extend a fragile US-Iran truce to cover Israeli military operations against Hezbollah. In a video message, Netanyahu declared, "There is no ceasefire. We are continuing to hit Hezbollah with force and we will not stop until we restore security," while also directing his cabinet to pursue direct negotiations with the Lebanese government aimed at disarming the militant group.

The statement came a day after Israel carried out its deadliest wave of strikes on Lebanon since the broader conflict began in early March, with the Israeli military saying it hit more than 100 Hezbollah command centers and military sites across Beirut, the Bekaa Valley, and southern Lebanon in just 10 minutes. Lebanon's health ministry reported at least 254 people killed and over 1,165 wounded in Wednesday's attacks, according to Al Jazeera. Several strikes hit densely populated commercial and residential areas in central Beirut without prior warning.

item.title: Trump says he's 'very optimistic' on Iran deal amid Lebanon crisis
item.description:
President Trump said Thursday he was "very optimistic" about securing a peace deal with Iran, even as massive Israeli strikes on Lebanon threatened to unravel a fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran that is only days old.

In a telephone interview with NBC News, Trump said Iranian leaders were "much more reasonable" in private negotiations than in their public statements, according to AFP. He added a warning: "If they don't make a deal, it's going to be very painful".

item.title: Iran's Khamenei vows revenge, signals 'new phase' at Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei declared on Thursday that Tehran would seek retribution for attacks on the country and move the management of the Strait of Hormuz into a "new phase," delivering a defiant message that threatens to upend a fragile ceasefire with the United States just days before critical peace talks in Pakistan.

item.title: Oil prices rebound as Iran accuses U.S. of ceasefire breach
item.description: A doubling of jet fuel prices since the outbreak of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran in late February has forced airlines worldwide to slash flights, raise fares, and hike baggage fees — reshaping the economics of air travel just as the summer season approaches. A fragile two-week ceasefire announced on Wednesday offered a glimmer of relief, but carriers are signaling that higher costs for travelers are here to stay.

item.title: OpenAI pitches compute edge over Anthropic as revenue gap widens
item.description:
OpenAI told investors this week that its early investments in computing infrastructure give it a key advantage over rival Anthropic at a moment when the smaller company is gaining ground in revenue and mulling a public offering, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.

The pitch comes as OpenAI faces mounting pressure from Anthropic, which disclosed on April 7 that its annualized revenue run rate has surpassed $30 billion — up from $9 billion at the end of 2025 and now exceeding OpenAI's most recently reported $25 billion figure. The number of Anthropic business customers spending more than $1 million annually has doubled from 500 in February to 1,000.

item.title: Forecasters warn potential super El Nino could reshape global weather by late 2026
item.description: Climate scientists and forecasting agencies are sounding alarms over what could become one of the strongest El Niño events in modern history, with models pointing toward a potential super El Niño developing in the second half of 2026 that would reshape weather patterns from India to California.

item.title: Trump demands Iran stop charging tolls on Hormuz strait
item.description: President Donald Trump on Thursday demanded that Iran cease imposing fees on oil tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz, writing on Truth Social that "They better not be and, if they are, they better stop now!" The warning further strained a fragile two-week ceasefire between Washington and Tehran, agreed to just two days earlier, under which Iran was supposed to fully reopen the critical waterway.

item.title: Starmer, Trump discuss plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer spoke with President Donald Trump on Thursday evening about developing a practical plan to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, calling from Qatar during a tour of the Gulf region aimed at shoring up the fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran.

item.title: Trump says he's 'very optimistic' about Iran deal as Vance heads to Islamabad
item.description:
President Donald Trump said Thursday he was "very optimistic" about reaching a peace deal with Iran, even as a two-day-old ceasefire showed signs of strain over continued Israeli strikes in Lebanon and disputes about the status of the Strait of Hormuz.

In a telephone interview with NBC News, Trump said Iranian leaders were "much more reasonable" in private negotiations than in their public statements, but warned that "if they don't make a deal, it's going to be very painful."

item.title: MIT develops silent artificial muscle fibers for robots
item.description: Researchers at the MIT Media Lab and Politecnico di Bari in Italy have developed a new class of artificial muscle fibers that operate silently and without motors, external pumps, or bulky hydraulic equipment — a breakthrough that could reshape how robots move and how wearable assistive devices are built.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire
item.description:
Russia and Ukraine have agreed to observe a 32-hour ceasefire over the Orthodox Easter weekend, with Russian President Vladimir Putin ordering his forces to halt combat operations "in all directions" starting Saturday, according to a Kremlin statement issued Thursday. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who had been pushing for such a truce for more than a week, agreed to the pause.

The ceasefire is set to begin at 4 p.m. Moscow time (1 p.m. GMT) on Saturday, April 11, and will last through the end of Easter Sunday, April 12. Defense Minister Andrei Belousov and Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov have been instructed to halt all military operations during the period.

item.title: Ecuador doubles tariffs on Colombia to 100% as trade war deepens
item.description:
Ecuador announced on Thursday that it will raise tariffs on all imports from Colombia to 100 percent, effective May 1, in the latest and most dramatic escalation of a trade war between the two Andean neighbors that has been building since January.

The government cited Colombia's "failure to implement concrete and effective border security measures" as justification for the increase, framing the levy as a sovereign response to drug trafficking along their shared border. "This measure is based on national security criteria and seeks to reinforce shared responsibility in a task that must be undertaken jointly to address the presence of drug trafficking at the border," the Ministry of Production, Foreign Trade, and Investment said in a statement.

item.title: Two fossil finds reshape understanding of life on land
item.description: Two fossil studies published this week are reshaping scientists' understanding of how land animals came to dominate Earth, with one revealing the oldest known rib-based breathing system in a 289-million-year-old mummified reptile and another providing the first direct evidence that mammal ancestors laid eggs some 250 million years ago.

item.title: Iran caps Hormuz transit at 15 ships a day under ceasefire
item.description:
Iran will permit no more than 15 vessels per day to transit the Strait of Hormuz under the two-week ceasefire it agreed with the United States, a senior Iranian source told Russia's TASS news agency on Thursday. The cap, enforced under the supervision of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, represents barely a tenth of the roughly 130 ships that crossed the waterway daily before the conflict began on 28 February.

"Under the current ceasefire, fewer than 15 ships per day are permitted to transit the Strait of Hormuz. This movement is strictly contingent upon Iran's approval and the enforcement of a specific protocol," the unnamed Iranian source said, adding: "There will be no return to the pre-war status quo."

item.title: Study finds low oxygen can trigger limb regeneration in mice
item.description: Salamanders and frog tadpoles can regrow entire limbs after amputation. Mammals cannot. A new study published April 8 in Science offers an explanation rooted not in genetics, but in how cells sense oxygen — and demonstrates that tweaking that response can awaken dormant regenerative programs in mouse tissue.

item.title: Xi Jinping meets Taiwan's KMT leader in Beijing
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Kuomintang Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Friday, marking the first meeting between a sitting KMT leader and China's Communist Party chief in nearly a decade. The encounter caps a week-long diplomatic push by Cheng, who has framed her six-day trip as a "journey for peace" aimed at easing military tensions across the Taiwan Strait.
